options: A folder for storing alarm history
A container that groups metrics by the AWS service that published them
A billing region
A type of alarm action
questions.explain: Namespaces like AWS/EC2 or AWS/ApplicationELB group metrics by their publishing service. Dimensions then scope a metric within that namespace to a specific resource.

questions.q: What does a CloudWatch 'dimension' let you do?
options: Change a metric's unit of measurement
Scope a metric to a specific resource, such as one EC2 instance or one load balancer
Delete old metric data automatically
Convert a metric into a log
questions.explain: Dimensions are name/value pairs (like InstanceId) that let you look at a metric for one specific resource instead of an undifferentiated average.

questions.q: When is an anomaly detection alarm a better fit than a static threshold alarm?
options: When a metric's normal range is constant and known in advance
When a metric's normal range shifts predictably by time of day or day of week
When you want to disable alerting entirely
Anomaly detection and static thresholds are functionally identical
questions.explain: Anomaly detection learns a metric's expected pattern over time and alarms when it leaves that learned band — better suited to metrics like traffic volume that vary predictably by time.

questions.q: A CloudWatch alarm was just created a minute ago and hasn't collected enough data points yet. What state is it in?
options: ALARM
OK
INSUFFICIENT_DATA
DELETED
questions.explain: INSUFFICIENT_DATA means the alarm doesn't yet have enough data to evaluate — common immediately after creation, and not itself a sign of a problem.

questions.q: What does the CloudWatch console's overview home page show?
options: Only billing information
Alarm state counts and metric graph widgets, refreshed automatically
A list of all IAM users
Source code for Lambda functions
questions.explain: The overview page surfaces alarm states and favorited metric graphs together so you can triage across services without navigating into each one individually.
